style: An Indonesian Si Kancil fable performed in warm, nimble, cinematic English. Keep the Indonesian name Si Kancil, pronounced see KAHN-chill. Let the comedy emerge from sincere danger, crocodile certainty, and exact counting rather than cartoon voices. Give every number in the two crossing lines a distinct physical landing. Do not add a moral. Leave a short natural breath after every line.

speakers.name: Narrator
speakers.style: A mature, textured storyteller with spacious visual phrasing, dry warmth, and crisp momentum during the crossing.

speakers.name: Si Kancil
speakers.style: Small, quick, observant, and genuinely frightened at first; composure arrives the instant the plan forms. Clever without smugness or a childish cartoon register.

speakers.name: The Brawny Crocodile
speakers.style: A large crocodile with a low, wet-edged authority; hungry, impatient, and absolutely confident in his own faulty logic without becoming a monster caricature.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: One afternoon, Si Kancil came to the narrow river on his way to visit his grandfather. Eight crocodiles dozed in the water.
lines.direction: Open on a humid, spacious afternoon; draw focus toward the narrow crossing and let eight land quietly but clearly.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: One crocodile was only pretending to sleep. An amber eye opened. “A kancil!” it cried, waking the river.
lines.direction: Begin as a close waterline secret; make the cry sudden and sharp, then widen its consequence across the whole river.

lines.speaker: The Brawny Crocodile
lines.text: Ha! Today, you will be our meal!
lines.direction: A deep, hungry declaration of victory; stress you without roaring or playing a cartoon villain.

lines.speaker: Si Kancil
lines.text: W-wait! If you eat me, how will you divide me fairly among all of you?
lines.direction: The first stammer is real fear; during the question, let fear become a deliberate invitation to greed.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The skinny crocodile complained that he always got the smallest piece. Soon, the river churned with an argument.
lines.direction: Dry, observant humor; widen the second sentence into noisy movement without muddying the narration.

lines.speaker: The Brawny Crocodile
lines.text: Enough! We shall count ourselves first. But… who can put the numbers in the right order?
lines.direction: Stop the quarrel with authority; after but, allow an embarrassed pause that reveals he cannot count either.

lines.speaker: Si Kancil
lines.text: I can. Line up from this bank to the other. I will count you from your backs.
lines.direction: Now completely calm and practical. Give the instructions as the obvious solution no one could reasonably suspect.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Snout to tail, the crocodiles stretched across the current—a living bridge of scales and teeth.
lines.direction: Begin close on bodies, then open wide on living bridge; let scales and teeth feel beautiful and dangerous.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: One—two—three—four. Si Kancil sprang from one broad back to the next while the crocodiles counted along.
lines.direction: Each number is its own light, precise landing; accelerate the sentence after the count without losing clarity.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Five—six—seven. “Eight!” the crocodiles shouted, delighted, as Si Kancil landed on the final back.
lines.direction: Let the first three numbers quicken; Eight is a delighted group shout, then settle gently on the final landing.

lines.speaker: The Brawny Crocodile
lines.text: Splendid! Now we can divide the kancil into eight equal pieces!
lines.direction: Thoroughly pleased that the problem is solved; remain oblivious to the final leap happening beyond his focus.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: But when they turned, Si Kancil had reached the far bank and vanished among the trees. Eight empty stomachs began a brand-new quarrel.
lines.direction: Give the reveal open, airy relief; close the last sentence with dry warmth and no spoken moral.
